jessica (sec-eng): Heads up — SBOM scan flagged a provenance mismatch for registry image redwood/runtime:2026-03-20. Missing signature header and KMS key audit shows rotation around the same time. I’ve quarantined the pushed artifact in s3://redwood-quarantine-01.
ajay (platform): Can you paste the SBOM diff and the registry push event? Might be the automated KMS rotation we did last night.
jessica (sec-eng): Paste from scanner: 
```
- provenance.signature: present
+ provenance.signature: missing
- signing.key.arn: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/oldkey
+ signing.key.arn: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/newkey
```
olivia (sre): @security-oncall I’m running an audit of who pushed that digest. Deploy-bot shows build id `ci-build-20260319-2312` from runner `ci-runner-12`. No external downloads yet.
deploy-bot: image push event: registry.redwood.ai/redwood/runtime:2026-03-20 by ci-runner-12, digest sha256:abcdef123456..., uploaded to s3://redwood-images/2026/03/20/runtime.tar.gz
ajay (platform): KMS logs: key rotation completed 2026-03-20T02:47:12Z. Rotation ID arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/newkey (previous key marked as non-current but not scheduled for deletion). The rotate was automatic per schedule. I don’t see any explicit revoke call.
security-oncall: Quarantine is good. Can we verify signature verification behavior when the key is non-current? If artifacts were re-signed with new key but SBOM kept old metadata, that would explain mismatch. I recommend P1 until validated.
jessica (sec-eng): Agreed P1. No CVEs in quick scan of deps, so impact likely limited to provenance. I opened incident INC-2026-0543 and added initial notes.
olivia (sre): Immediate containment: remove push/write permissions for principal `ci-runner-12` and rotate CI service token. Also enable stricter RBAC on registry. Ajay, can you push a deny rule? :lock:
ajay (platform): Applying temp deny via terraform patch now — registry_policy block for principal `ci-runner-12`. PR: https://github.com/redwood/platform/pull/4321 (will link once CI passes). Rotating CI token and invalidating current creds.
jessica (sec-eng): Also need to update audit logging to capture KMS Verify and Sign calls to the central log (90d retention) and surface them in console. That will help correlate future rotations.
ajay (platform): On it. Creating a follow-up config change to forward KMS CloudTrail Verify/Sign events to logging bucket with 90d retention. Will include alert rule.
security-oncall: Next steps checklist: 1) reproduce signature verification against both keys locally, 2) re-run SBOM generation from the build artifact (if available) and compare hashes, 3) if mismatch persists, rebuild from source and re-sign, 4) review RBAC for all CI runners, 5) post-incident writeup.
jessica (sec-eng): I’ll take 1–3. Olivia please coordinate the RBAC and token rotation. Ajay to finish logging change. I’ll add remediation notes to INC-2026-0543.
olivia (sre): Will do. Quick Q: do we want to re-publish the image automatically after rebuild or keep it quarantined until legal signs off?
security-oncall: Keep quarantined until we have signature provenance validated. If rebuild from source is clean, we can mark as safe after audit. Inform legal only if any exfil or suspicious actor is suspected.
ajay (platform): Terraform deny applied and token rotation complete. Logging PR opened. I’ll also add a temporary CloudWatch alarm for any future SBOM-signature failures for the next 48h.
jessica (sec-eng): Thanks all — I’ll post updates in the incident ticket. Ping me if any test fails. :mag:
security-oncall: Noted. I’ll monitor and escalate if we see similar mismatches across other images in the next 24h. :eyes:
